messages:
oncall-bot: :warning: ALERT: Elevated container restart rate in eu-central-1 GPU pool (symptom=prefill_cuda_oom). Detected restarts=22 in 8m for runtime-serving. Paging oncall. incident_tag=2837654321

simon: picking this up. I'm oncall now. Assessing impact and gathering logs. @priya @lucas please stand by.

priya: looking at traces — a small set of requests with huge context sizes (~45k-120k tokens) are lining up and causing memory climbs during prefill. Observed linear allocation growth until cudaMalloc fails.

lucas: cluster snapshot: 8 GPU nodes, 6 ready, 2 in transient NotReady (gpu-node-9 shows repeated GPU resets). Pod failures mostly on gpu-node-9 and some spillover on gpu-node-3.

qa-bot: reproduced locally: run with a long QA prompt (estimate 80k tokens) into the same model -> allocation spikes then CUDA OOM. Behavior matches production.

priya: logs (abridged):
```
[2026-03-15T09:18:05Z] prefill: req=def456 ctx_est=83421 allocate=20.4GiB -> cudaMalloc returned out of memory
[2026-03-15T09:18:06Z] runtime: process terminated due to SIGKILL (oom)
[2026-03-15T09:18:07Z] kubelet: container runtime restarted container runtime-serving-def456
```

lucas: nvidia-smi dump (gpu-node-9): GPU0 79G/80G, GPU1 8G/80G. Large python process pinned to GPU0. Driver shows GPU reset events.

simon: mitigation options ranked quick->safe: 1) emergency admission limit for prefill tokens (hard cap at 32k) 2) immediate routing of >24k requests to redwood-medium-quant with strict memory quota 3) cordon gpu-node-9 and force drain to stop repeated resets 4) enable prefill streaming to avoid large contiguous allocations (longer rollout).

priya: applying emergency cap now to minimize blast radius: set runtime config prefill_max_tokens=32768 and policy=truncate-right for 45m. Executing via configmap update.

deploy-bot: Applying runtime config patch...
```
kubectl -n prod patch configmap runtime-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"prefill_max_tokens":"32768","prefill_truncation":"truncate-right"}}'
```
deploy-bot: patch successful (obj/runtime-config hash=ff3344).

lucas: also creating routing override rule to send requests with token_estimate>24000 to redwood-medium-quant (quantized) and to set request_mem_limit=10Gi.

```
# routing override (pseudo)
if request.token_estimate > 24000 -> model=redwood-medium-quant, runtime_mem_limit=10Gi
```

infra-bot: cordon initiated for gpu-node-9. `kubectl cordon gpu-node-9` then `kubectl drain gpu-node-9 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Pods rescheduled. Note: cluster has limited spare capacity; expect short increased scheduling latency.

simon: customer impact check: pulling API key access logs. Looks like 4 external API keys experienced 5xx spikes; one is a paying customer (ACME-Prod). Time window ~09:12-09:20 UTC. Error rate for long-context endpoints peaked at 18% 5xx.

cs-bot: draft customer message: "We detected an infrastructure issue affecting long-context requests in eu-central-1 between 09:12-09:22 UTC. We applied temporary limits and routing to restore stability. We'll follow up with a detailed report." Approving send?

emma (CS): sending now.

lucas: after config and routing changes, restart rate reduced from 22 -> 3 over 10m. A few residual failures occurred as pods rebalanced. GPU resets on gpu-node-9 stopped after drain.

priya: collecting artifacts for postmortem: previous container logs, `dmesg` from gpu-node-9, GPU driver logs, and a gcore of the process where possible. Uploading to s3://redwood-incidents/2837654321/ for analysis.

```
kubectl logs -n prod -p runtime-serving-def456 > /tmp/def456-prev.log
dmesg | grep NVRM > /tmp/gpu-reset.log
aws s3 cp /tmp/def456-prev.log s3://redwood-incidents/2837654321/def456-prev.log
```

lucas: initial hypothesis: large single-request prefill allocations combined with fragmentation in the KV cache and cluster memory pressure led to repeated cudaMalloc failures and subsequent GPU resets. We should add accounting to block any single-request allocation > X% of GPU memory and increase reserved headroom per node.

simon: immediate follow-ups assigned: priya -> implement hard guardrail in prefill allocator + better logging; lucas/infra -> evaluate autoscale and standby spare GPUs; runtime team -> add adaptive prefill streaming to reduce contiguous allocations; product -> consider guiding customers about recommended context sizes and opt-in batch processing for extremely large contexts. I'll own the incident writeup.

deploy-bot: Incident state update -> mitigated. incident_id=2837654321 status=mitigated

simon: closing the live thread. If new restarts surface, page infra/sre. Otherwise I'll open the PCR and assign owners. :white_check_mark:
